Workspace allocator with size classes, superblock management, free, compact, and diagnostics.

# Purpose
`fd_alloc` implements a workspace-backed memory allocator with support for small and large allocations, alignment control, and concurrent use. It stores allocator state in an `fd_alloc_t` object inside a workspace, uses size classes for small allocations, and uses direct workspace allocation for large requests. The file defines the allocator layout, allocation headers, superblock management, and helper functions for choosing size classes and concurrency groups. It also provides the public lifecycle APIs [`fd_alloc_new`](<#fd_alloc_new>), [`fd_alloc_join`](<#fd_alloc_join>), [`fd_alloc_leave`](<#fd_alloc_leave>), and [`fd_alloc_delete`](<#fd_alloc_delete>), plus query functions such as [`fd_alloc_wksp`](<#fd_alloc_wksp>), [`fd_alloc_tag`](<#fd_alloc_tag>), [`fd_alloc_align`](<#fd_alloc_align>), [`fd_alloc_footprint`](<#fd_alloc_footprint>), and [`fd_alloc_superblock_footprint`](<#fd_alloc_superblock_footprint>).

The main allocation logic is in [`fd_alloc_malloc_at_least`](<#fd_alloc_malloc_at_least>) and [`fd_alloc_free`](<#fd_alloc_free>). Small allocations come from superblocks that are split into blocks, while large allocations are taken directly from the workspace. The file also manages active superblock slots and inactive superblock stacks, with atomic operations when available and fallback single-threaded code when not. In addition, it includes diagnostic and maintenance functions such as [`fd_alloc_compact`](<#fd_alloc_compact>), [`fd_alloc_is_empty`](<#fd_alloc_is_empty>), and [`fd_alloc_fprintf`](<#fd_alloc_fprintf>), which scan allocator state and print detailed information about superblocks, blocks, and workspace usage.
